# Answer: **734**

We count the positive integers from 1 to 999 and remove those divisible by 6, 10, or 15.

## Define the sets

- A = multiples of 6
- B = multiples of 10
- C = multiples of 15

## Single sets

$$|A| = \left\lfloor \tfrac{999}{6} \right\rfloor = 166,\quad |B| = \left\lfloor \tfrac{999}{10} \right\rfloor = 99,\quad |C| = \left\lfloor \tfrac{999}{15} \right\rfloor = 66$$

## Pairwise intersections

A number divisible by two of these is divisible by their least common multiple:

- lcm(6, 10) = 30
- lcm(6, 15) = 30
- lcm(10, 15) = 30

So each pairwise intersection is the set of multiples of 30:

$$|A\cap B| = |A\cap C| = |B\cap C| = \left\lfloor \tfrac{999}{30} \right\rfloor = 33$$

## Triple intersection

lcm(6, 10, 15) = 30, so

$$|A\cap B\cap C| = 33$$

## Inclusion–exclusion

$$|A\cup B\cup C| = (166 + 99 + 66) - (33 + 33 + 33) + 33$$
$$= 331 - 99 + 33 = 265$$

## Complement

$$999 - 265 = \boxed{734}$$

So 734 positive integers less than 1000 are divisible by none of 6, 10, or 15.
